inevitable_need: Before an agent opens a PR on a production service, something automatically feeds it the decisions and past incidents that apply to that code, the stuff we keep re-explaining in architecture review that isn't in the repo or the CLAUDE.md, and blocks the merge if it touches something a human has to sign off on.
why_inevitable: Agents are already writing a growing share of our PRs, and sooner or later one of them will ship a change that repeats an outage we already had a postmortem for. After that I can't defend 'the agent didn't know' to the CEO, and a hand-maintained CLAUDE.md doesn't scale past a dozen services.
must_have: Runs inside our own infra or VPC, so incident history and Slack data never leave it
Plugs into the agents we already use through MCP or a pre-PR hook with no workflow change, and every claim it makes cites a source
Proven to catch real repeats: on our own history it flags the incidents and constraints a senior engineer would have flagged
deal_breakers: Per-engineer seat pricing that I have to defend to finance as yet another line item
Hosted-only or still-in-preview handling of our incident and Slack data with no SSO or data-retention terms
Noisy briefings that pad the agent's context with generic or uncited stuff, so they make the agent worse or slower
expected_provider: Most likely my own team builds a thin version first (vector DB, an MCP server, a postmortem ingester), and within a year or two the agent makers like Anthropic or Cursor ship org-level memory themselves. I'd only pay a startup if its open-source core is clearly better than my weekend build and they sell support or enterprise features on top.
memoryworks_would_need: Show me on our own self-hosted install, inside a month, that a briefing stopped an agent from repeating a real past incident. Then sell a flat per-org enterprise tier, with SSO, audit logs, a data-retention policy security will sign and support, for the self-hosted version instead of $20 a seat for a hosted preview.
